title: Decision seats start on a fresh probe and rotate like card seats
status: in progress (corrective for MD-002 after audit flag F-070); code in mob-defaults

decisions.slice: window 226-slice: SHIP AS IS (slice f0c0d63, amended 4bb7d00)

claude_seat_reason: probes at 01:20 UTC show Codex, Copilot, Grok and agy without usable quota
metric: decision seats seated on a stale probe or out of rotation (target 0); Claude share of decision seats while others had capacity

intent.line: Intent: the product owner wants decision seats (Decider voters and objection-window seats) to rotate like card seats, and the runner to enforce it: in the owner's D163 words, "I just want the rotation to even out and don't just jump to all Claude like has happened in the past". D164 chose least-recently-used rotation as the mechanism (a Claude seat refused only while another available model has waited longer, no ratio cap), and each seat starts on a probe under 60 minutes old. Why: audit flag F-070 (audits 56 and 57) found decision seats in decider.py still run with no fresh-probe check, no rotation and no recorded reason, which leaves MD-002 open; this card applies card 208's rules to decision seats so load cannot pile onto Claude unseen.

against: D163 (the product owner's words, quoted verbatim)
D164 C1 (least-recently-used rotation, no ratio cap)
confirmation.note: restates recorded direction and adds no scope

domain_expert.reason: the change applies card 208's rules inside decider.py, covered by the architect and backend developer
the risks are the listed loopholes; the gate runs in the main thread before any worker starts

Criterion 2 is least-recently-used seating over card 208's rotation rules, the check_seat and commit_seat split of gate_seat, pending lines for the voters of one run and an append-only seat-use history, all code and git semantics the architect, QA engineer, backend developer and independent reviewer already hold; criterion 1 showed the card 208 code could be reused through CardRun without a second copy and with no process or Windows problem beyond hygiene already handled (decider.py CRLF kept; scratch cleanup unchanged). The one open choice, whether a Claude voter is judged after the non-Claude voters of the same run, is a reading of D163 and D164 for the reviewer and the Intent confirmation, not outside knowledge. A member can still be added mid-card through a Decider (with its id).

adjustment_reviews.adjustment: Card 219 stand-down 1 adjustment, first use (three parts): (1) MOB.md regenerated at fixed steps (when the green seat is launched and when a green is reported), with 'MOB.md non-MOB commits since regeneration: n' printed in the seat-start line; (2) the D165 intent line and its confirmation in one commit; (3) each in-flight stamp from date -u run at the commit it rides in, and a suite run gets its own wait line citing its seat-start line.
adjustment_reviews.issue: Card 219's criterion 1 green was held by MOB.md being 6 non-MOB commits stale (maximum 3); the intent line and its confirmation took two commits; one of three in-flight stamps was typed and later than its own commit.
adjustment_reviews.evidence: (1) Held greens: 0 (target 0; the green body and the push record no staleness hold, and main = origin/main). Green 2189ca2 (02:30:16Z) came with 0 non-MOB commits since the last regeneration (a57a5d0, 02:11:36Z; the record commit 9f42b70 followed the green). Fixed steps were run: 112a630 (01:54:04Z) 40 s after red 8357f14 and 67 s before the developer's seat-start line, which prints 0; a1d62bd (02:31:10Z) 54 s after the green. But the 0 at the green was not earned by the two fixed steps alone: between 112a630 and the green the wait produced fba2ab1 (seat-start line), 4945a99 (suite line), c8d92ee (the path correction) and 4aee027 (probe evidence), 4 non-MOB commits, over the maximum of 3, and the facilitator regenerated a third time, ad hoc (a57a5d0), at 02:11:36Z. Regeneration commits this cycle: 3 (112a630, a57a5d0, a1d62bd; counter-metric limit 'more than 3 is churn', so at the limit; 4 if 7f0284b after the slice is counted). The suite line (4945a99, 02:08:37Z) prints 'since regeneration: 0' where git shows 1 (fba2ab1): the count was typed. (2) One commit, 52d4676 (01:45:16Z), carries the Intent line and the confirmation (21 inserted lines in one file), against two commits on card 219 (bca5510, e4cda78): resolved. (3) Stamps against own commit: QA 01:44:36 vs 05d6448 01:44:37Z; developer 01:55:11 vs fba2ab1 01:55:11Z; suite 02:08:37 vs 4945a99 02:08:38Z: exact, 3 of 3 with seconds. The architect's slice line is stamped '01:36 UTC' (no seconds) and its commit 21a9f79 is 01:35:58Z, so that stamp is typed and 2 s later than its commit: 1 of 4 lines (card 219: 1 of 3). Probe ages against the probe rows (01:20:30Z to 01:20:40Z): architect 16 (arithmetic 15), QA 24 (24), developer 36 (35), suite line 53 where the arithmetic is 48 min (02:08:37Z minus 01:20:40Z; 4aee027 puts it at 50 at 02:10): 1 of 4 off by more than a minute. Caps: 4 of 4 name a source; the suite line's source is measured ('last measured 1258 s plus 10 min'; the run took 1268.8 s and finished at 02:29:59Z, 10 min 38 s before the cap), the other three still 'the seat brief'. The suite line has its own wait line but names no seat-start line (it matches ctx-4 only by role and card). Red to green 36 min 52 s (01:53:24Z to 02:30:16Z), of which the whole suite was 21 min 10 s; card 219 was 10.7 min on a 311-test suite in another repository, so not like for like.
adjustment_reviews.side_effects: Good: no green held; one intent commit instead of two; stamps with seconds are exact. Bad: the staleness result depended on an unplanned regeneration, so the fixed steps do not by themselves cover a 21-minute wait in which the facilitator commits three times; a typed count (0 for 1) and a typed probe age (53 for 48) show the printed numbers are only as good as the typist; each regeneration is a commit (3 this cycle).
adjustment_reviews.verdict: tune ((2) keep as is; (1) and (3) keep their steps but the printed numbers come from commands, not typing: the count from git rev-list --count since the last MOB.md commit, the probe age from the newest probe row, and the stamp from date -u with seconds, including on a slice line; and a regeneration also when the printed count reaches 3 during a wait. This is the one adjustment of this stand-down).
